A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

comment.comment:
$ORBIO | The Cost of Privacy. And the Value of Trust. 🪐

I've just shared my thoughts on @0x_aster's latest article, The Cost of Privacy.

And I believe it reveals something important about where @orbiodotso is heading.

For months, we've been watching Orbio evolve from an AI credit marketplace into a broader inference infrastructure platform.

Now the team is exploring a potentially more defensible business model.

Not just selling AI cheaper. Building AI that people can actually trust.

Yash's article goes beyond marketing promises. It examines encryption, secure enclaves, hardware verification, and the limitations that still exist.

What caught my attention is the willingness to acknowledge those limitations.

Because privacy shouldn't depend entirely on someone saying, "Trust us."

It should become increasingly verifiable.

And if Orbio can make that protection accessible without sacrificing usability, it could have something genuinely valuable.

But as an investor, I still want to see the next step:
• Users choosing Orbio for its privacy
• Recurring payments beyond free credits
• Sustainable infrastructure economics
• Clear value creation for $ORBIO holders

The technology is becoming more ambitious. Now the business needs to prove itself.

I continue holding $ORBIO, and the long-term thesis remains alive.

I published my full perspective on X, including why I think trust could become more valuable than competing on discounts.

👇 Read my quote-post:
https://x.com/Vlad007T/status/2118609748119474605

A discount can be copied. Trust has to be earned. 🪐

comment.comment:
onchain will rise again 🛡️🌅

tl;dr: short term stock + crypto market gets uglier. when btc turns, liquidity flows back down the curve, and zcat is set up to be a top meme of the cycle.

the setup
- btc/crypto likely bleeds more short term. onchain naturally bleeds harder
- but liquidity has historically cascaded the same way: equities → btc → majors → alts → top memes → trenches
- onchain hasn't stayed dead once btc finds strength or trades sideways. i don't think this time is the exception

why zcat
- reflections turn a memecoin into a cash-flowing bag where whales don’t have to sell: 3% tax on every trade, paid to holders in $ZEC
- $9.1M in ZEC distributed to zcat holders so far
- zcat is the #1 reflection by a wide margin [mcap/holders]
- category leaders run first and hardest when the tide comes back

why this time is different
- past cycles, memes ran to billions while new money had to learn uni/jup/aero, bridge, scan X all day for signals, dodge rugs, and pray for CEX listings

fomo / pump / terminals removed all of it:
- liquidity abstracted: no stables stranded across chains and L2s
- social built in: discovery and conviction in one feed
- traders are now chain agnostic: one app, no bridging, no dex-hopping

same liquidity waterfall + a fraction of the friction + more buyers with apps focused on user acquisition 

the bet
- no guarantees but personally i think zcat is a top 3 meme this cycle
